claim: Worked examples beat conventional problem solving for novices learning algebra-like procedures; classroom evidence (Zhu and Simon 1987) shows large gains in one school (93.1 vs 75.5 post-test, p<.001) and a ceiling null in another (97.2 vs 95.1).
agent_test: Subgoal library with worked solutions vs problems-only prompts on novel procedural tasks at equal tokens, easy vs hard split.

claim: The pooled human effect is medium: the published Barbieri et al. (2023) meta-analysis of math worked examples reports g = 0.48 (43 articles, 55 studies, 181 effect sizes, robust variance estimation). The g = 0.43 (40 articles, 49 studies) figure was not found in the journal text and is treated as an earlier version. Publication-bias tests could not be checked.
agent_test: Treat as prior only; run own effect-size estimate on agent tasks with several seeds.

claim: Early geometry and kinematics studies failed to show the effect because of split attention; integrating text and diagram restored it.
schema_part: G#/S# layout: keep solution steps adjacent to the diagram/data they refer to
agent_test: Compare split vs integrated example formatting in prompts at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Expertise reversal: for learners with prior knowledge, worked examples help less or hurt compared with problems.
agent_test: Gate example retrieval by estimated difficulty: show examples only when the first attempt fails or the task is novel.

claim: Adaptive fading (removing solved steps as competence grows) beat fixed example-problem pairs in a lab study but only partly in a classroom replication (delayed transfer only). Update: a review of eight tutored studies (Salden 2010) finds examples added to a strong tutor mainly save time (5 of 8) and help long-term retention (3 of 3 tested); exact Ns for Schwonke 2009 and Salden 2009 still not retrieved.
agent_test: Fade subgoal-library hints across repeated attempts; compare with static hints.

claim: Self-explanation prompts amplify what is learned from examples; in the meta-analysis they moderated the effect negatively, so the direction is unsettled. Update: Barbieri 2023 finds the prompt moderator negative in math; Wittwer and Renkl 2010 find added instructional explanations minimal (21 studies).
agent_test: Add or drop an explain-the-step instruction when reading a stored example.

claim: In LLMs, demonstrations act largely through format, label space and input distribution; random labels cost only 0-5 points (1.7 multi-choice, 2.6 classification average).
agent_test: Replace stored solutions with format-only stubs and measure drop.

claim: Chain-of-thought exemplars are the LLM analogue of worked examples: GSM8K 17.9 to 56.9 (PaLM 540B) and 15.4 to 48.5 (text-davinci-002).
agent_test: Worked-solution exemplars vs answer-only exemplars on held-out math.

claim: Exemplar logical validity matters less than relevance and coherence: invalid-reasoning exemplars kept about 81% of CoT accuracy (39.5 vs 48.5) while no-relevance fell to 11.0 and no-coherence to 23.1.
schema_part: memory: retrieve for relevance and ordered structure first
agent_test: Corrupt step correctness vs corrupt relevance in the stored subgoal examples.

claim: Model-written correct solutions can replace human solutions: Reinforced ICL plateaus near 25 examples and is about 5 points above human-solution ICL on MATH500; unsupervised (problems only) matches or beats solutions.
schema_part: memory: self-generated verified solutions populate the library
agent_test: Fill library from own verified solves; compare with hand-written ones.

claim: More examples can hurt: human-solution ICL peaks near 125 shots then declines on MATH500; reasoning models reportedly degrade with few-shot (DeepSeek-R1, one sentence, no data).
agent_test: Sweep k=0,1,2,4,8 retrieved examples with a reasoning model at fixed token budget.

claim: Skill-matched in-context examples help hard questions but hurt easy ones (GSM8K easy 96.3 fixed vs 83.2 skill-based); adaptive use recovers gains up to 3.6 points (AdaptMI) and 6 (AdaptMI+).
agent_test: Show examples only after a failed or low-confidence first attempt (the expertise reversal analogue).

claim: Self-generated exemplars equal or beat retrieved ones on large models (GSM8K 5-shot CoT 75.0 vs 75.8-77.8) but not on small ones (curie about 2-3% for all).
agent_test: Self-generate analogous solved problems before solving; check on small vs large model.

claim: Agent skill and workflow libraries built from solved episodes improve agents: Voyager diamond pickaxe 19 vs 36 iterations without library; AWM +24.6% Mind2Web, +51.1% WebArena; self-generated examples ALFWorld 73 to 89.
agent_test: Ablate the library at equal tokens, on tasks with train-test gap.

claim: Insights extracted only from the original few-shot examples gave ExpeL no advantage over ReAct; benefit comes from new experience, not re-reading the seed examples.
agent_test: Compare library built from own experience vs seeded only.

claim: LLM-generated worked examples for students: ChatGPT help gave learning gains comparable to human tutor help in one study (N=274), human hints better in another (N=77); about 32% of generated help failed quality checks.
agent_test: Quality-gate stored examples with a verifier before inclusion.

claim: No source directly runs the CLT design (examples vs bare problems, matched load) for LLM agents. The nearest tests compare stored full solutions in context against no examples: for reasoning models they hurt (d01), for strong instruct models they add nothing beyond format (d03), for weaker models they help. This is a measured analogue, not the CLT effect.
agent_test: Run a direct example-vs-problem test with matched token budgets.

claim: Reasoning-class models are hurt by full worked solutions in context: one retrieved CoT demo cost about 6 to 16 AIME-2025 points and three cost up to 35; on GPQA Diamond 1 to 8 points. DeepSeek-R1 authors also say few-shot degrades it (no data). Converting demos to short insights removed the harm (R1-Distill-14B AIME 50.0 to 60.0).
agent_test: Store distilled subgoal notes, not traces; test raw trace vs note at equal tokens on a reasoning model.

claim: LLM expertise-reversal analogue: exemplars help weak or base models and format, but give no gain to strong instruction-tuned models (Qwen2.5-72B GSM8K 95.75 8-shot vs 95.83 fixed zero-shot; MATH 81.30 vs 81.64). The threshold is ragged (some 1.5B to 3B models do better zero-shot). Pattern-induction tasks show direct beats CoT by 5.10 points on average.
agent_test: Switch example use on by measured baseline competence per skill, not by default.

claim: Correctness gating matters for a stored library: adding every self-generated experience dropped scores below a small fixed memory (EHRAgent 16.75 to 13.05) while strict-checked adds gave 38.50; history-based deletion gave a further gain on some tasks. Self-generated successful trajectories lifted ALFWorld 0.73 to 0.89. Human math data agree: correct examples alone beat mixed (Barbieri).
agent_test: Admit entries only after a verifier passes; retire entries by outcome history.

claim: Number of retrieved examples: relevance-selected sets peak early (about 5 to 20 in classification) and extra examples can lower scores for most models; agent work used k = 6 to 10 without a k sweep. Reasoning-model results use k = 1 or 3 only. No source here sweeps k = 1, 2, 4 for subgoal libraries.
agent_test: Run a k sweep of 1, 2, 4 with relevance ranking at equal tokens.

claim: Open gaps after the gap search: no open source gives exact Ns or effect sizes for Sweller and Cooper 1985, Schwonke 2009 or Salden 2009; no test of explain-then-use prompts on stored solutions for LLMs; no LLM analogue of adaptive fading; no 2024-2026 study with learner test scores for LLM-generated worked examples. Barbieri publication-bias tests unknown.
agent_test: Treat these as unknown, not as null results.
